patients.summary: Retired factory worker with COPD on triple inhaled therapy, a 42 pack-year current smoking habit and a 2018 LEEP for HPV-related cervical dysplasia. Invasive vaginal squamous cell carcinoma found in October 2023 and treated with radiation; a COPD exacerbation sent her to the ED in September 2025.

First available new-patient slot 6/8 at 9:20 accepted. Release of information signed over the phone and sent to her old office for the last five years of notes, labs and imaging. Asked her to bring the inhalers themselves to the visit.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
61 y/o woman establishing care; her prior PCP retired. Main issue is COPD, which she says was named about seven years ago after a winter of bronchitis that never quite cleared. Gets winded on a flight of stairs or carrying laundry up from the basement, better than it was before she was on the current inhalers. No hospital stays for her lungs. Uses albuterol a few times a week, mostly in humid weather.

Inhalers (brought in): fluticasone/salmeterol 250/50 one puff BID, tiotropium 18 mcg capsule daily, albuterol HFA PRN. Technique on the disk inhaler is decent; she forgets to rinse sometimes.

GYN: abnormal Pap with high-risk HPV in 2018, LEEP that year for dysplasia, followed since by her own gynecologist. Postmenopausal, no bleeding. Tubal ligation at 32.

Allergies: sulfa (rash); latex (contact dermatitis).

Family: mother died at 67 of cervical cancer; father died at 71 of lung cancer; sister had breast cancer at 55.

Social: retired from factory work, on disability. Divorced, lives alone. Smokes, roughly 42 pack-years total. Knows it is the reason for her breathing and says she 'thinks about it' but isn't ready to commit to anything. No alcohol, no drugs.

Exam: thin, comfortable at rest, speaking full sentences. HEENT unremarkable. Neck supple, no nodes. Lungs: diminished at both bases, prolonged expiration, no wheeze or crackles. Heart RRR, no murmur. Abd soft, nontender. Ext without edema or clubbing. Skin: no rash.

A/P
1. COPD on LABA/ICS plus LAMA, stable. Continue all three. Rinse after the steroid inhaler. No spirometry in what she remembers; will look for it in the old records.
2. Tobacco: 5 minutes spent on cessation. Contemplative. Offered patch, varenicline, quitline; she will think it over.
3. Lung cancer screening: qualifies. Low-dose CT ordered; discussed what a positive or incidental finding would mean.
4. Breast: screening mammogram ordered, last one she thinks two years ago.
5. HPV / prior LEEP: cervical follow-up stays with her gynecologist.
6. Health maintenance: CBC, CMP, lipids, A1c, one-time hep C and HIV today. Vaccines: will catch up this fall.
Return in about 6 months, sooner if needed.

Your old records came in too; the colonoscopy from 2016 was clean and isn't due again until 2026. The radiology scheduler should call about the CT. Take care.

reports.study: Low-dose CT chest for lung cancer screening
reports.text:
Indication: Lung cancer screening, current smoker, 42 pack-years. Baseline exam.
Technique: Low-dose helical CT of the chest without IV contrast.
Findings: Mild centrilobular emphysema, upper-lobe predominant. No pulmonary nodules. Airways patent. No consolidation or effusion. Heart size normal; no pericardial effusion. No mediastinal or hilar lymphadenopathy. Visualized upper abdomen unremarkable. No suspicious osseous lesion.
reports.conclusion: Lung-RADS 1: negative. Continue annual screening in 12 months.

reports.text: Bilateral CC and MLO views with tomosynthesis. Comparison: none available. Breasts are scattered areas of fibroglandular density. No suspicious mass, architectural distortion or suspicious calcifications. Skin and nipples unremarkable.

documents.body:

O: Vitals as charted. Lungs with distant breath sounds, no wheeze. Heart regular. No edema.
A/P: COPD, stable on triple therapy. No spirometry anywhere in her old records, so ordering full PFT-lab spirometry with bronchodilator to document the baseline. Smoking: revisited; she agrees cigarettes are the problem but 'not right now.' Gave the quitline card again. Flu, PCV20 and booster done in October. RTC 6 months for wellness visit.

reports.text: Pre- and post-bronchodilator spirometry, albuterol 4 puffs via spacer. Effort and reproducibility acceptable (ATS/ERS criteria met, 3 acceptable maneuvers). Post-bronchodilator FEV1/FVC 0.58. Post-bronchodilator FEV1 61% predicted. No significant bronchodilator response. Flow-volume loop with concave expiratory limb.
reports.conclusion: Moderate airflow obstruction without significant reversibility, consistent with COPD.

documents.title: Spirometry interpretation
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Ratio 0.58 post-BD with FEV1 61% predicted: moderate fixed obstruction, fits her COPD. No change to inhalers; she already takes LAMA plus LABA/ICS. Will go over it at the wellness visit. Message sent to patient.

Problems: COPD (spirometry 3/2022 FEV1/FVC 0.58, FEV1 61%), tobacco dependence, high-risk HPV with LEEP 2018, tubal ligation.
Meds: fluticasone/salmeterol 250/50 BID, tiotropium 18 mcg daily, albuterol PRN. Allergies sulfa (rash), latex (dermatitis).
Breathing steady; albuterol twice a week. No bleeding or discharge; sees her gynecologist yearly.
Exam: BP and weight as charted. Lungs diminished, no wheeze. Heart RRR. No edema.
Screening plan: LDCT due this month (baseline 6/2021 Lung-RADS 1); mammogram due; colonoscopy 2016 normal, next 2026; cervical care with GYN. Tdap today. Shingrix: she'll get the series at her pharmacy. Labs today.
Tobacco: advised to quit, contemplative, declines meds for now.
Advance directive: she will think about naming her sister as proxy; forms given.
RTC 6 months.

reports.study: Low-dose CT chest for lung cancer screening
reports.text:
Indication: Annual screening, current smoker. Comparison: 6/23/2022 and 6/29/2021.
Technique: Low-dose helical CT without contrast.
Findings: Stable mild centrilobular emphysema. No nodules, masses or consolidation. No pleural effusion. Mediastinum and hila without adenopathy. Coronary arteries without significant calcification. Upper abdomen unremarkable.

documents.title: Mammogram result

documents.title: Bleeding question
documents.author: patient
documents.body: I didn't want to bring it up at the shot visit. Since sometime in July I've had spotting off and on, which I haven't had in years since the change, and a discharge that smells bad. It doesn't really hurt, just feels uncomfortable down there. Should I see you or go straight to my gynecologist? I'd rather start with you.

documents.title: RE: Bleeding question
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thank you for telling me, this needs to be looked at soon. Bleeding after menopause always gets checked. The front desk will call you Monday with a visit early next week, and I'll get you to gynecology quickly from there. If the bleeding gets heavy, go to the emergency room.

orders.reason: postmenopausal bleeding, malodorous discharge, prior LEEP and high-risk HPV

documents.title: Office visit - postmenopausal bleeding
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
CC: vaginal bleeding and discharge.
HPI: 63 y/o, menopausal for years, with on-and-off spotting for about three months and a foul-smelling discharge over the same stretch. Not much pain, more a feeling of pelvic discomfort. No fever. No urinary symptoms reported. History of high-risk HPV with LEEP for dysplasia in 2018. Mother had cervical cancer. Smoker.
She called her own gynecology office last week; they had nothing for six weeks.
Exam: well appearing. Abdomen soft, nontender, no masses. She asked to have the pelvic exam done once by the gynecologist rather than twice; reasonable given she can be seen within days.
A/P: Postmenopausal bleeding with malodorous discharge in a woman with HPV and prior LEEP. Needs speculum exam and tissue promptly. Called the gynecology group directly and got her in on 10/11. Referral and last note faxed. Return precautions for heavy bleeding. Will follow.

documents.title: Gynecology visit
documents.author: gynecology
documents.body:
Outside gynecology office note, date of service 10/11/2023, received by fax 10/13/2023.

Reason: intermittent vaginal bleeding x 3 months with malodorous discharge. Minimal pain; pelvic discomfort.
Hx: COPD; HR-HPV; LEEP for cervical dysplasia at 58; BTL at 32. Meds: fluticasone/salmeterol, tiotropium, albuterol PRN. Allergies: sulfa (rash), latex (contact dermatitis) - non-latex gloves and speculum used. FHx: mother cervical cancer, father lung cancer, sister breast cancer. Smoker, 42 pk-yr.
Exam: Irregular ulcerated lesion of the posterior vaginal wall. Biopsy obtained, hemostasis with pressure.
Plan: await pathology; will call patient and PCP. Gyn-onc referral if malignant.

conditions.label: Malignant neoplasm of vagina
conditions.note: invasive squamous cell carcinoma, posterior vaginal wall

reports.text:
Specimen: Vagina, posterior wall, biopsy.
Gross: Received in formalin, two tan-pink soft tissue fragments, aggregate 0.6 x 0.4 x 0.2 cm, entirely submitted in one cassette.
Microscopic: Squamous mucosa with atypical squamous cells showing invasion into the subepithelial connective tissue.
reports.conclusion: Vagina, posterior wall, biopsy: invasive squamous cell carcinoma.

documents.title: Pathology - vaginal biopsy
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Pathology report from the gynecology group's lab, signed 10/16/2023, faxed to PCP as copy recipient. Routed to PCP urgent.

documents.title: Call with patient re: biopsy
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Called pt after the gynecologist had already given her the result yesterday. She knows it is a cancer of the vagina. Tearful but organized. Gynecology has referred her to gynecologic oncology; first appointment next week, scans to be scheduled through them. Answered what I could; told her I'd follow along and she can call any time. Added to problem list. She asked if smoking played a part; told her it can, and that stopping helps treatment go better. She said she'd think about it.

documents.title: Gynecologic oncology letter
documents.author: gynecologic oncology
documents.body:
Dear colleague,
I saw Ms. Mayhew on 10/25/2023 for biopsy-proven invasive squamous cell carcinoma of the posterior vaginal wall. Allergies: sulfa, latex.
Staging: MRI pelvis shows the tumor confined to the vaginal wall without extension beyond it; no enlarged pelvic or inguinal nodes. PET/CT shows no nodal or distant disease. FIGO stage I.
Recommendation, agreed with radiation oncology at tumor board: definitive radiation, external-beam pelvic treatment followed by vaginal brachytherapy, to begin 11/13. We will see her in surveillance after treatment.
Thank you for involving us.
Gynecologic oncology

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up after cancer treatment
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Here to catch up after radiation. Per her account: pelvic external-beam treatment daily from mid-November, then brachytherapy sessions, finished 1/19. She says she got through it and the team was good to her. First gyn-onc surveillance visit is in April. No summary from radiation oncology yet; records requested.
Breathing: stable through the winter, no extra steroids, rescue inhaler 2-3 times a week. Still smoking, cut down 'a few' during treatment, back to usual now.
Exam: vitals as charted. Lungs with decreased breath sounds, no wheeze. Heart RRR. Abdomen soft, nontender.
A/P
1. Vaginal SCC, stage I, s/p definitive radiation - surveillance with gyn-onc. Basic labs today.
2. COPD stable - continue inhalers.
3. Tobacco - advised again; contemplation. She will call if she wants to try the patch.
Wellness visit in May.

documents.title: Records request - radiation oncology

documents.title: Radiation oncology treatment summary

Radiation treatment summary. Diagnosis: squamous cell carcinoma of the vagina, FIGO stage I. Allergies: sulfa, latex.
Course: external-beam radiation to the pelvis, 45 Gy in 25 fractions, 11/13/2023 to 12/18/2023, followed by vaginal brachytherapy, completed 1/19/2024. Treatment completed as planned.
Follow-up: gynecologic oncology surveillance; radiation oncology as needed.

documents.title: Emergency department note
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
ED provider note, visit 9/29/2025, faxed to PCP 9/30.
65F with COPD, high-risk HPV, and vaginal SCC diagnosed 10/2023 s/p radiation, here with worsening shortness of breath over a couple of days, more than her baseline. Home meds: fluticasone/salmeterol 250/50 BID, tiotropium 18 mcg daily, albuterol PRN. Allergies: sulfa (rash), latex (contact dermatitis). Current smoker.
SpO2 91% RA on arrival. Albuterol/ipratropium nebulizer given; SpO2 95% RA afterward and breathing eased.
Impression: acute exacerbation of COPD.
Dispo: home on prednisone 40 mg daily x 5 days; continue home inhalers; PCP follow-up within a week. Before discharge she acknowledged her smoking has caused her problems but felt it was likely too late to stop now.

documents.title: Call after ED visit

documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seen in the ED 9/29 for a COPD flare (short ED note received: SpO2 91% on arrival, 95% after a neb; sent home on prednisone 40 mg x 5 days). Finished the steroid on 10/3. Breathing is back to her normal now; walking around the house and to the car without trouble. Using maintenance inhalers daily.
Watched her use both inhalers: disk technique good; with the capsule device she was not breathing in hard enough to rattle the capsule, corrected and she repeated it well.
Exam: speaking full sentences, no distress. Lungs diminished, no wheeze. Heart RRR. No edema.
A/P
1. COPD exacerbation, resolved. Continue current inhalers. Written action plan reviewed: when to use albuterol more, when to call.
2. Tobacco: she told the ED it's too late to quit. We talked it through again - quitting still reduces flares. Offered varenicline or patches with quitline support; she declined both today. Remains contemplative.
3. Flu and COVID vaccines at the nurse visit later this month.
RTC in a few months.

documents.title: Gynecologic oncology follow-up
documents.author: gynecologic oncology
documents.body:
Surveillance visit 7/14/2026. Diagnosis: squamous cell carcinoma of the vagina, FIGO stage I, definitive radiation completed 1/2024. Allergies: sulfa, latex. Medications per patient: fluticasone/salmeterol, tiotropium, albuterol.
Exam today without evidence of recurrence. No evidence of disease.
Plan: continue surveillance every 6 months. Smoking cessation encouraged.
